title: JSON Schema dialect
description: The rule that schemas default to JSON Schema 2020-12 unless a `$schema` field declares another dialect, such as draft-07.
question: Does the framework honour the declared dialect, or assume one?
why: Dialects disagree about details that change validation outcomes. A framework that assumes 2020-12 will mis-handle a draft-07 schema that says so explicitly, and the resulting failures look like the server sent a bad schema.
known_issues: Measured by scripts/measure_protocol.py: each adapter runs against fixtures/base_protocol_server.py behind the wire recorder, and the cell is read from the captures.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: one draft-07 tool with tuple-form `items` (a list) makes MCPServerAdapter fail to load the whole server (`'list' object has no attribute 'get'` in crewai/utilities/pydantic_schema_utils.py). With that tool left out, the 2020-12 tool is rebuilt through Pydantic: `$schema` and `dependentRequired` are dropped, `prefixItems` becomes `items: {}`, and `$defs` is renamed.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` copies only `properties`, `required` and `additionalProperties`, so `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `dependentRequired` are dropped, leaving any `$ref` into them dangling.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `load_tools` rebuilds `parameters` from `properties` and `required` only, so `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `dependentRequired` are dropped. Properties that point at a dropped `$defs` entry keep a dangling `$ref`.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): with either dialect tool listed, the adapter loads no tool at all. `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each schema as a Pydantic model, and `McpToolSpec._resolve_field_type` fails on both: the 2020-12 tool's boolean subschema (`"items": false`) raises `TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable`, and the draft-07 tool's tuple `items` list raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. `to_tool_list_async` builds every tool in one loop, so one such tool fails the listing for the whole server, over stdio and Streamable HTTP. Without both, the other three tools load and are called normally.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: both dialect tools are listed and called, but `toGeminiSchema` drops what has no genai `Schema` field: `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `$ref` (the referenced `window` arrives as an empty object), 2020-12 `prefixItems` and `dependentRequired`, and draft-07 tuple `items` and `additionalItems`. Same over stdio and Streamable HTTP (`data/measurements/protocol/google_adk_js/run.json`).
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): a tool whose `inputSchema` is valid draft-07 but not valid 2020-12 (tuple-form `items`) fails the whole listing: `haystack.tools.Tool` checks every `parameters` with `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` and raises `ValueError: The provided parameters do not define a valid JSON schema`, and `MCPToolset.warm_up` builds every tool in one pass, so no tool loads. The 2020-12 tool kept all eight dialect keywords.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt inlines every `$ref` with `jsonref.replace_refs` and drops `$defs`, and keeps only `inputSchema.properties`, so `$schema`, `definitions` and the 2020-12 tool's `dependentRequired` are gone. `prefixItems`, `items: false` and tuple `items` survive. Because smolagents marks every property required, a 2020-12 call that omits the optional `label` is rejected before it reaches the server (`Argument label is required`).
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: `convert_input_schema_to_tool_args` keeps only the `inputSchema` properties, inlining `$defs` references. `$schema` and top-level keywords such as `dependentRequired` are dropped, and a draft-07 `definitions` block is dropped with its `$ref`s left dangling.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `JSONSchemaModel.create` runs `simplify_json_schema`, which calls `.items()` on a property's `items` value. A 2020-12 boolean `"items": false` raises `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'items'`, and a draft-07 tuple-form `items` list fails the same way, when the agent builds its system prompt. The `RequirementAgent` run then fails for every tool, not only the one with the schema.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime rewrites keywords it does not pass to the provider into description text. In the 2020-12 tool, `dependentRequired` becomes `{dependentRequired: {"label":["units"]}}` on the schema's description and `items: false` becomes `{"description": "{schema: false}"}`; in the draft-07 tool the tuple `items` becomes an `anyOf` and `additionalItems: false` likewise turns into a description. `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions`, `$ref` and `prefixItems` pass through.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): both dialect tools are offered, but each goes through `create_model_from_schema` and the strict OpenAI schema. The draft-07 tool's tuple `items` fails the Pydantic build, and `MCPToolResolver` logs `Failed to build args schema` and registers the tool with an empty `properties` object, so the model is offered none of its parameters. The 2020-12 tool loses `$schema` and `dependentRequired`, `prefixItems` becomes `items: {}`, and `window`'s `$ref` is inlined. The derived evidence reads "not offered" because the protocol instrument's long launch command pushes every name past 64 characters, so `sanitize_tool_name` hashes away the MCP tool name the cell matches on; the schemas above were read from the same capture in listing order.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. The model has no `$schema`, `definitions`, `dependentRequired`, `prefixItems` or `additionalItems`, so both the 2020-12 and draft-07 dialect markers and their keywords are dropped.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: both dialect tools are left out of the registry. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` catches any `Throwable` from `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` and only logs it, so a tool it cannot parse is left out of the `ToolRegistry`. The 2020-12 tool's `items: false` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Element class kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonLiteral is not a JsonObject`, and the draft-07 tool's tuple-form `items` throws the same for `JsonArray`.
